title: Site-wide timeouts from core database connection pool exhaustion
symptoms: Checkout, booking and login requests timed out at once. Logs showed pool checkout timeouts and core-db active connections at the maximum.
root_cause_summary: A scheduling-api scale-out doubled its replica count, and each replica opened a full connection pool against core-db.
resolution: Scaled scheduling-api back to its previous replica count and cancelled long-running queries. Connections recovered within 6 minutes.

postmortem.summary: A routine scale-out exhausted core-db connections and took down every tier-1 service that reads from the database for 22 minutes.
contributing_factors: Connection pool size was set per replica with no global cap
No alert on core-db connections approaching the maximum

action_items.description: Add an alert at 80% of core-db maximum connections
Size pools from a shared connection budget instead of per replica

title: Booking reminders delayed by SMS provider rate limiting
symptoms: SMS reminders arrived up to 40 minutes late. Notifications queue depth grew steadily and logs showed 429 responses from the SMS provider.
root_cause_summary: A reminder batch for a large business customer exceeded the SMS provider's per-second rate limit, and failed sends were retried immediately.
resolution: Added backoff to SMS retries and spread the batch over 20 minutes. The queue drained in 35 minutes.

postmortem.summary: Immediate retries against a rate-limited SMS provider kept the notifications queue growing until backoff was added.
contributing_factors: Retries had no backoff
Large batches were sent at the full queue rate

action_items.description: Retry SMS sends with exponential backoff on 429 responses
Throttle reminder batches per customer

title: Provider search missing new providers after stalled index rebuild
symptoms: Newly onboarded providers did not appear in web app search results for most of a day. Search latency and error rate were normal.
root_cause_summary: The nightly search-index rebuild from core-db stopped at a malformed provider record, so the index stopped picking up new providers.
resolution: Skipped the malformed record, restarted the rebuild and backfilled the missing providers.

postmortem.summary: A single bad record halted index rebuilds silently. Only web app search was affected; bookings and checkout were not.
contributing_factors: The rebuild job stopped on the first bad record
No alert on index rebuild lag

action_items.description: Skip and report malformed records instead of stopping the rebuild
Alert when index rebuild lag exceeds 2 hours

title: Internal 401s after auth mTLS certificate expired
symptoms: A sudden spike in 401 Unauthorized responses from auth at a round time, with TLS handshake failures from internal callers. There was no auth deploy.
root_cause_summary: The internal mTLS server certificate for auth expired. Its renewal had been done by hand and the reminder was missed.
resolution: Issued and deployed a new certificate, then restarted auth pods one at a time. 401s stopped within 4 minutes of the rollout.

postmortem.summary: An expired internal certificate made auth reject every internal caller. Logins, bookings and checkout failed for 31 minutes.
contributing_factors: Certificate renewal was manual
No alert before certificate expiry
Auth logged the expiry but no one watched those logs

action_items.description: Automate internal certificate renewal
Alert 14 days before any internal certificate expires

title: Monthly invoices stuck in pending after a malformed plan record
symptoms: Business customers reported missing monthly invoices. The invoice job failed repeatedly in billing logs and invoices stayed pending.
root_cause_summary: A plan record with a missing currency field crashed the invoice job, which then retried the same batch forever.
resolution: Fixed the plan record, released the stuck batch and re-ran the invoice job. All invoices were generated the same day.

postmortem.summary: One malformed plan record blocked the whole monthly invoice run for 9 hours.
contributing_factors: The invoice job processed every customer in one batch
Plan records were not validated on write

action_items.description: Process invoices per customer so one failure doesn't block the rest
Validate plan records when they are saved

title: Card authorizations failing during card processor outage
symptoms: Payment authorizations failed across all card types. payment-gateway logged timeouts and errors calling the card processor. No recent payment-gateway deploy.
root_cause_summary: The external card processor had a regional outage. payment-gateway itself was healthy but could not authorize cards.
resolution: Waited for the processor to recover and paused deposit-required bookings in the meantime. Authorizations recovered after 48 minutes.

postmortem.summary: An outage at the card processor blocked every deposit checkout. Nothing on the Fernhill side had changed.
contributing_factors: Single card processor with no fallback
Customers saw a generic error instead of a retry message

action_items.description: Show a clear retry message when the card processor is unavailable
Evaluate a secondary card processor

title: Bookings missing from external calendars after provider token expiry
symptoms: New bookings did not appear in providers' external calendars, and calendar-sync job lag grew for 3 hours.
root_cause_summary: OAuth tokens for one external calendar provider expired in bulk, and calendar-sync retried without refreshing them.
resolution: Refreshed the tokens, replayed the backlog and contacted providers whose calendars had double bookings.

postmortem.summary: Expired calendar tokens stalled sync for one external calendar provider and caused a handful of double bookings.
contributing_factors: calendar-sync did not refresh tokens on a 401 from the provider
No alert on sync job lag

action_items.description: Refresh calendar tokens on 401 responses
Alert when calendar-sync lag exceeds 30 minutes

title: Blank booking page in one mobile browser after front-end release
symptoms: Browser errors spiked right after a web-app release. The booking page was blank in one older mobile browser; backend APIs were healthy.
root_cause_summary: The release used a JavaScript feature that one older mobile browser doesn't support.
resolution: Rolled web-app back to the previous release, then re-released with the feature transpiled.

postmortem.summary: A front-end release broke booking for a small share of mobile users for 50 minutes.
contributing_factors: Browser support targets were not enforced in the build

action_items.description: Enforce browser support targets in the front-end build

title: Stale booking reads during core database replica lag
symptoms: Bookings and payments went missing for a few seconds after creation, then appeared. core-db replica lag peaked at 40 seconds.
root_cause_summary: A bulk data backfill on core-db generated more write traffic than the replicas could apply.
resolution: Paused the backfill and routed read-after-write queries to the primary until lag recovered.

postmortem.summary: A backfill caused replica lag, and customers saw their new bookings disappear briefly. Some booked twice.
contributing_factors: Backfills had no write-rate limit
Read-after-write paths read from replicas

action_items.description: Rate-limit backfill jobs on core-db
Read booking confirmations from the primary

title: Checkout 5xx errors from a pricing rule null reference
symptoms: checkout-api 5xx rate rose to 6% and customers saw "something went wrong" at checkout. Latency was normal.
root_cause_summary: A new pricing rule with no end date triggered a null reference in checkout-api's discount calculation.
resolution: Disabled the pricing rule, then shipped a fix that treats a missing end date as open-ended.

postmortem.summary: A configuration change, not a deploy, broke checkout for customers whose cart matched the new pricing rule.
contributing_factors: Pricing rules were not validated against checkout-api's assumptions

action_items.description: Validate pricing rules before they go live

title: Mass logouts after session signing key rotation
symptoms: Users were logged out and had to sign in again right after the scheduled key rotation. Token validation errors mentioned an unknown key ID.
root_cause_summary: The new session signing key was activated before it reached every auth instance, so tokens signed with it failed validation elsewhere.
resolution: Re-published the key set to every auth instance and kept the previous key valid for 24 hours.

postmortem.summary: A key rotation that skipped the overlap period logged out most active users. Certificates were not involved.
contributing_factors: Key rotation did not keep the previous key valid during rollout

action_items.description: Keep the previous signing key valid for 24 hours after rotation

title: Receipt emails delayed by notifications queue backlog
symptoms: Payment receipts and invoice emails arrived up to an hour late. Notifications queue depth grew for 50 minutes.
root_cause_summary: A notifications worker deploy halved the worker count by mistake, so the queue grew faster than it drained.
resolution: Restored the worker count. The backlog cleared in 25 minutes.

postmortem.summary: Half the notifications workers were missing after a deploy. Emails were late but none were lost.
contributing_factors: Worker count lived in the deploy manifest with no review

action_items.description: Alert when notifications queue depth grows for 10 minutes

title: Checkout latency from a long-running migration holding core-db connections
symptoms: checkout-api p95 latency rose above 2 seconds and payment-gateway slowed too. There was no checkout-api or payment-gateway deploy.
root_cause_summary: A schema migration on core-db held long transactions open, and queries from checkout-api and payment-gateway waited for connections.
resolution: Cancelled the migration and re-ran it in small batches overnight.

postmortem.summary: Checkout looked like the problem, but both checkout services were waiting on core-db during a migration.
contributing_factors: Migration ran during peak traffic
Migrations were not batched

action_items.description: Run large migrations in batches outside peak hours

title: Slow provider search after the synonym list grew
symptoms: Provider search p95 rose to 900 ms in the web app. Other pages were normal.
root_cause_summary: A large synonym list update made every search query expand to hundreds of terms.
resolution: Reverted the synonym list and re-applied a trimmed version.

postmortem.summary: A data change slowed web app search. Booking, checkout and login were unaffected.
contributing_factors: Synonym list changes were not load tested

action_items.description: Load test synonym list changes before publishing

title: Double bookings when scheduling-api skipped calendar-sync events
symptoms: Providers reported double bookings. New bookings were missing from external calendars although calendar-sync was healthy.
root_cause_summary: A scheduling-api change stopped publishing booking events for rescheduled appointments, so calendar-sync never received them.
resolution: Rolled scheduling-api back, then replayed the missed events to calendar-sync.

postmortem.summary: The problem looked like a calendar-sync stall, but the events were never sent.
contributing_factors: No end-to-end check that every booking reaches calendar-sync

action_items.description: Add a reconciliation job comparing bookings with synced calendar events

title: Checkout button broken after front-end release
symptoms: Customers could not complete checkout from the booking page. Browser errors spiked after a web-app release; checkout-api showed no errors because requests never reached it.
root_cause_summary: A web-app release renamed a form field, and the checkout button handler threw before sending the request.
resolution: Rolled web-app back to the previous release.

postmortem.summary: A front-end bug looked like a checkout outage, but checkout-api and payment-gateway were healthy throughout.
contributing_factors: No end-to-end checkout test in the front-end release pipeline

action_items.description: Add an end-to-end checkout test to the web-app release pipeline

title: SMS confirmations failed after notifications template deploy
symptoms: SMS booking confirmations failed right after a notifications deploy. Email was unaffected and no other service reported errors.
root_cause_summary: A notifications template change exceeded the SMS provider's message length limit, and the provider rejected every message.
resolution: Rolled notifications back to the previous version and shortened the template.

postmortem.summary: A notifications deploy broke only notifications. Booking itself kept working; customers just didn't get a text.
contributing_factors: Templates were not checked against the SMS length limit

action_items.description: Check SMS templates against the provider's length limit in CI

title: Duplicate invoices sent after billing job retried
symptoms: Business customers received two copies of their monthly invoice email.
root_cause_summary: The invoice job timed out after sending emails but before recording them, then retried and sent them again.
resolution: Voided the duplicate invoices and emailed affected customers a correction.

postmortem.summary: A non-idempotent retry in billing sent duplicate invoices to 140 business customers.
contributing_factors: Invoice sends were not idempotent

action_items.description: Make invoice sends idempotent with a per-invoice send key

title: Payment gateway slow responses during card processor degradation
symptoms: payment-gateway and checkout-api p95 latency rose for 35 minutes. The card processor's response time had tripled. No recent payment-gateway deploy.
root_cause_summary: The external card processor was degraded and slow to respond. payment-gateway waited on it up to its timeout.
resolution: Waited for the card processor to recover. Lowered the processor timeout to fail faster during the event.

postmortem.summary: Slow checkouts were caused outside Fernhill: the card processor was degraded and nothing had been deployed.
contributing_factors: payment-gateway timeout to the card processor was 5 seconds
No dashboard separating processor latency from gateway latency

action_items.description: Show card processor latency separately on the payment-gateway dashboard

title: Checkout latency after payment-gateway deploy added a synchronous fraud check
symptoms: checkout-api p95 latency climbed to 2.1 seconds about 10 minutes after a payment-gateway deploy. payment-gateway p95 rose with it. Other services and the card processor were healthy.
root_cause_summary: payment-gateway v3.6.0 added a synchronous fraud-score lookup to the card authorization path and raised the processor timeout, so every checkout waited on the slow lookup.
resolution: Rolled payment-gateway back to v3.5.4 with `fernctl rollback payment-gateway --to previous`. checkout-api p95 recovered within 5 minutes of the rollback.

postmortem.summary: A payment-gateway deploy made card authorization wait on a fraud-score lookup. Checkouts slowed for 28 minutes until the rollback. Paged payments-primary.
contributing_factors: The fraud-score lookup ran synchronously in the authorization path
The deploy was not load tested at peak traffic
Raising the processor timeout hid the slowdown from timeout alerts

action_items.description: Alert on payment-gateway p95 within 10 minutes of any deploy
Load test the authorization path before payment-gateway deploys
Move the fraud-score check off the synchronous authorization path

title: Checkout errors for zero-decimal currencies
symptoms: checkout-api 5xx rate rose above 1% for customers paying in zero-decimal currencies. Latency was normal.
root_cause_summary: A checkout-api deploy multiplied amounts by 100 for every currency, and payment-gateway rejected the out-of-range amounts.
resolution: Rolled checkout-api back and added currency-aware rounding.

postmortem.summary: A rounding bug in checkout-api failed checkouts in two currencies for 2 hours.
contributing_factors: Tests covered only two-decimal currencies

action_items.description: Add zero-decimal currency cases to checkout-api tests

title: Full outage when a retry storm exhausted core database connections
symptoms: Every tier-1 service timed out at once. core-db active connections were at the maximum and logs showed "too many connections" errors.
root_cause_summary: A brief core-db failover triggered client retries with no jitter, and the retries opened connections faster than core-db could serve them.
resolution: Shed load at the web-app edge, restarted the worst clients one at a time, then restored traffic gradually.

postmortem.summary: The longest outage on record: 41 minutes with every customer-facing flow down.
contributing_factors: Client retries had no jitter or budget
No load shedding at the edge

action_items.description: Add jittered retries with a retry budget to every core-db client
Add load shedding at the web-app edge

title: Calendar sync lag after provider API rate limit change
symptoms: calendar-sync job lag grew to 2 hours for one external calendar provider. Other providers synced normally.
root_cause_summary: The external calendar provider lowered its API rate limit, and calendar-sync batches were too large to stay under it.
resolution: Lowered the sync batch size for that provider. Lag recovered over 90 minutes.

postmortem.summary: A third-party rate limit change slowed calendar sync. Bookings themselves were unaffected.
contributing_factors: Batch size was the same for every calendar provider

action_items.description: Make sync batch size configurable per calendar provider

title: Invoice totals briefly stale during replica failover
symptoms: Invoice previews showed old totals for a few seconds after plan changes. core-db replica lag peaked at 12 seconds.
root_cause_summary: A planned core-db replica failover left one replica catching up while it served reads.
resolution: Removed the lagging replica from the read pool until it caught up.

postmortem.summary: A planned failover caused short-lived stale reads in billing. No invoices were wrong.
contributing_factors: Replicas joined the read pool before catching up

action_items.description: Hold replicas out of the read pool until lag is under 1 second

title: Token validation failures from an unknown key ID after rotation
symptoms: 401s rose across web-app, checkout-api and scheduling-api right after a scheduled key rotation. Errors mentioned an unknown key ID. Certificates were valid.
root_cause_summary: The key set cache in auth clients kept the old key set for an hour, so tokens signed with the new key failed validation.
resolution: Flushed the key set cache in every auth client, then lowered its TTL.

postmortem.summary: A stale key set cache after rotation looked like an auth outage. It was fixed without touching certificates.
contributing_factors: Key set cache TTL was longer than the rotation overlap

action_items.description: Lower the key set cache TTL to 5 minutes
Refetch the key set on an unknown key ID

title: Search errors during full index rebuild after tokenizer upgrade
symptoms: web-app search returned 504s and search-index p95 rose above 2 seconds after a search-index deploy started a full rebuild. Checkout and booking were normal.
root_cause_summary: A tokenizer upgrade triggered a full index rebuild, and queries hit partially built shards.
resolution: Served queries from the previous index until the rebuild finished.

postmortem.summary: A full rebuild degraded search for 70 minutes. Impact was limited to web app search.
contributing_factors: Rebuilds swapped the index in place instead of building alongside it

action_items.description: Build new indexes alongside the live one and switch when complete

title: Provider profile pages blank after front-end release
symptoms: Provider profile pages rendered blank after a web-app release. Backend APIs were healthy.
root_cause_summary: The release referenced an image component that was missing from the production bundle.
resolution: Rolled web-app back, fixed the bundle configuration and re-released.

postmortem.summary: A bundling mistake blanked provider profiles for 25 minutes.
contributing_factors: The production bundle was not smoke tested

action_items.description: Smoke test key pages against the production bundle before release

title: Reminder emails delayed by email provider throttling
symptoms: Reminder emails arrived up to 30 minutes late. The email provider returned rate-limit errors and queue depth grew.
root_cause_summary: The email provider throttled Fernhill's account during a large reminder batch.
resolution: Spread the batch over a longer window and asked the provider to raise the limit.

postmortem.summary: Email reminders were late but delivered. SMS and booking were unaffected.
contributing_factors: Email batches were not throttled like SMS batches

action_items.description: Throttle email batches the same way as SMS batches

title: Invoice PDFs missing tax line after billing deploy
symptoms: Business customers reported invoices without a tax line after a billing deploy. Invoice generation itself succeeded.
root_cause_summary: A billing template change dropped the tax line for customers on annual plans.
resolution: Rolled billing back and regenerated affected invoices.

postmortem.summary: A template regression in billing produced incorrect invoices for annual-plan customers.
contributing_factors: Invoice templates had no snapshot tests

action_items.description: Add snapshot tests for invoice PDFs

title: Checkout 5xx from expired pricing cache entries
symptoms: checkout-api 5xx rate rose to 3% with no change in latency. Errors began when the pricing cache refreshed.
root_cause_summary: checkout-api treated an empty pricing cache entry as an error instead of reloading it from core-db.
resolution: Restarted checkout-api pods to repopulate the cache, then shipped a fix to reload empty entries.

postmortem.summary: A cache edge case in checkout-api failed checkouts for 15 minutes.
contributing_factors: Cache misses were handled as errors

action_items.description: Reload empty pricing cache entries instead of failing
